rules.when: The task is visual, browser-driven, or product-facing UI work.
rules.why: Keep visual work on its preferred profile, and move it to the other family only while that provider is unavailable.

rules.when: The task is architecture, security-sensitive, or deep diagnosis work.
rules.why: Preserve the strongest reasoning class on both tiers; an outage must never quietly downgrade it.

rules.when: The task is a substantial or bounded non-visual implementation.
rules.why: Ordinary implementation work continues on the other family at a comparable effort while one provider is down.

rules.when: The task is deterministic mechanical work such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, or targeted typo fix.
rules.why: A locally hosted model belongs on this rule's primary tier once it has completed harness verification; until then keep a cheap verified profile here.

rules.when: The task is an independent review or audit of work another family produced.
rules.why: Review keeps the opposite-family requirement and waits when it cannot be met, rather than letting a family review its own work.
